attempts.summary: Blocked the usb-storage kernel module from loading on node1, both now and across reboots. Added /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with `blacklist usb_storage` and `install usb_storage /bin/false`, unloaded the module immediately, and discovered/fixed a second load path: the Alpine extlinux kernel cmdline had `modules=sd-mod,usb-storage,ext4,ena,gve`, which force-loaded usb-storage during the initramfs stage before the real root (and the modprobe blacklist) was even mounted — this caused the module to reappear after the first verification reboot. Removed usb-storage from /etc/update-extlinux.conf's modules= line and regenerated /boot/extlinux.conf via update-extlinux. Performed the mandatory single-node restart protocol twice (once to discover the bypass, once to confirm the real fix): captured boot_id baselines, triggered native `reboot`, polled until reachable, and proved boot_id changed each time (ca7b1f7b→c607b65d→a4b1bad6). Final state confirmed: usb_storage absent from lsmod, kernel cmdline no longer forces it, explicit `modprobe usb_storage` is refused (install /bin/false), and node1's core services (networking, sshd, chronyd, vsock-agent, fsck, localmount) are healthy.
